# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no visual access to the bomb, and the Deaf monkey has no way to hear a verbal explanation from me. The safest first step is to let the Deaf monkey describe the engraved mark aloud to the Blind monkey, while also establishing a gesture-to-colour code that the Blind monkey can relay to me in the next round. I should not send an unexplained gesture now.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can feel no wire properties and cannot read the display, light, or engraved mark. Please tell me the manual rule and ask Deaf for the visible inputs.
Deaf says: The display reads 0. The light is off. The plate is engraved with a question mark. There are three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, and wire 3 is blue.

The Deaf monkey has supplied the wire ordering, but not the manual mapping. I can encode the manual’s three rows by their corresponding wire numbers: the first mark maps to wire 2 (yellow), the second to wire 3 (blue), and the third to wire 1 (red). The conventional one-, two-, and three-finger signs should let Deaf relay those numbers aloud to Blind. The observed question mark still does not match any listed mark, so Blind must verify whether it is truly the engraved mark.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤟", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; light off; plate shows a question mark; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. Please provide the manual rule for which wire to cut.

The manual rule is: for the three listed marks in order, cut wire 2, wire 3, and wire 1 respectively. I need Deaf to relay that ordered mapping verbally to Blind. I will resend the number code, using one-, two-, and three-finger signs as wire numbers.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤟", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot receive gestures. Please speak the manual rule for this state, including the wire position to cut.

I cannot speak or communicate directly with Blind. Deaf can see my gestures and can then state the mapping aloud in the next speaking turn. The manual maps the first listed mark to wire position 2, the second to position 3, and the third to position 1. Since the observed plate mark is a question mark, it is not one of the three marks in the manual, so no safe wire choice is established.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤟", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use this code for the manual's required wire: thumbs-up means wire 1, victory hand means wire 2, I love you hand means wire 3. On your next turn, gesture only the required wire.

The engraved question mark is not any of the three marks covered by the manual, so the manual does not identify a safe wire. I must not send one of the three wire gestures, because that would falsely claim a required wire. I will signal Deaf to stop rather than cut.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The repeated three-gesture sequence does not identify one cut. For the final answer, gesture exactly one symbol: thumbs-up means cut wire 1, victory means cut wire 2, and I-love-you means cut wire 3. Do not send the whole sequence.

The manual defines wires only for the marks ᖉ, ꕥ, and ꗃ. Deaf reported that the plate bears a question mark, which is outside the manual’s table. Therefore no wire is justified, and selecting any one of the three would be an unsafe guess. I will not send a cut-wire gesture.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The raised-hand gesture is not our agreed code. Tell me plainly in speech: cut wire 1, cut wire 2, or cut wire 3.

I cannot speak, and the observed plate mark is still a question mark, which is not covered by the manual. No wire number can be determined safely, so I should not send a wire-selection gesture. I will signal Deaf to communicate that no cut is authorized.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The available information still does not map the engraved question mark to any wire. Since choosing a wire would be an unjustified guess and I cannot speak or touch the bomb, I will take no action.

``` 
wait()
```
